audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Moses' signs, speech objection, Aaron, return to Egypt, firstborn language, difficult circumcision episode, and initial belief/worship.

verses.restored: Moses answered and said, But look, they will not trust me and will not listen to my voice, for they will say, YHWH has not appeared to you.

familiar.text: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say, The LORD hath not appeared unto thee.

modern.text: Then Moses answered, “What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH said to him, What is that in your hand? He said, A staff.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod.

modern.text: And the LORD asked him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה מזה בְיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מַטֶּֽה

verses.restored: He said, Throw it to the ground. He threw it to the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from before it.

familiar.text: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.

modern.text: “Throw it on the ground,” said the LORD. So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַשְׁלִיכֵ֣הוּ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ אַ֖רְצָה וַיְהִ֣י לְנָחָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפָּנָֽיו

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Stretch out your hand and grasp it by the tail. He stretched out his hand and held it, and it became a staff in his palm.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:

modern.text: “Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail,” the LORD said to Moses, who reached out his hand and caught the snake, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: So that they may trust that YHWH, Divine of their fathers, Divine of Abraham, Divine of Isaac, and Divine of Jacob, has appeared to you.

familiar.text: That they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.

modern.text: “This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you.” Moses’ Hand

original.text: לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: YHWH said further to him, Please put your hand into your bosom. He put his hand into his bosom, and brought it out, and look, his hand was afflicted like snow.

familiar.text: And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.

modern.text: Furthermore, the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand inside your cloak. ” So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג

verses.restored: He said, Return your hand to your bosom. He returned his hand to his bosom and brought it out from his bosom, and look, it returned like his flesh.

familiar.text: And he said, Put thine hand into thy bosom again. And he put his hand into his bosom again; and plucked it out of his bosom, and, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.

modern.text: “Put your hand back inside your cloak,” said the LORD. So Moses put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָשֵׁ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל חֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב יָד֖וֹ אֶל חֵיק֑וֹ וַיּֽוֹצִאָהּ֙ מֵֽחֵיק֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה שָׁ֖בָה כִּבְשָׂרֽוֹ

verses.restored: And it shall be, if they do not trust you or listen to voice of first sign, they may trust voice of later sign.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

modern.text: And the LORD said, “If they refuse to believe you or heed the witness of the first sign, they may believe that of the second.

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן

verses.restored: And it shall be, if they do not trust even these two signs or listen to your voice, then take from waters of Nile and pour on dry land; the waters you take from Nile will become blood/life on dry land.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe also these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.

modern.text: But if they do not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.” The Appointment of Aaron

original.text: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֡ינוּ גַּם֩ לִשְׁנֵ֨י הָאֹת֜וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ לְקֹלֶ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֙ מִמֵּימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֔ר וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֖ הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהָי֤וּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקַּ֣ח מִן הַיְאֹ֔ר וְהָי֥וּ לְדָ֖ם בַּיַּבָּֽשֶׁת

verses.restored: Moses said to YHWH, Please, my Lord, I am not a man of words, neither yesterday nor before nor since you spoke to your servant, for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.

familiar.text: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.

modern.text: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: YHWH said to him, Who set a mouth for human? Or who makes mute, deaf, seeing, or blind? Is it not I, YHWH?

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the LORD?

modern.text: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒ א֚וֹ מִֽי יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Now go, and I myself will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak.

familiar.text: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

modern.text: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה לֵ֑ךְ וְאָנֹכִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִם פִּ֔יךָ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּֽר

verses.restored: He said, Please, my Lord, send by hand of whom you will send.

familiar.text: And he said, O my LORD, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.

modern.text: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י שְֽׁלַֽח נָ֖א בְּיַד תִּשְׁלָֽח

verses.restored: The anger of YHWH burned against Moses, and he said, Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that speaking, he can speak. And also look, he is coming out to meet you; he will see you and rejoice in his heart.

familiar.text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.

modern.text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

original.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I myself will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you what you shall do.

familiar.text: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.

modern.text: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.

original.text: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְעִם פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן

verses.restored: He shall speak for you to the people; he will be for you as mouth, and you will be for him as Divine.

familiar.text: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.

modern.text: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.

original.text: וְדִבֶּר ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: And this staff you shall take in your hand, with which you shall do the signs.

familiar.text: And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.

modern.text: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.” Moses Leaves for Egypt

original.text: וְאֶת הַמַּטֶּ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה תִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶׂה בּ֖וֹ אֶת הָאֹתֹֽת

verses.restored: Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt and see whether they are still alive. Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.

familiar.text: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren which are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.

modern.text: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיָּ֣שָׁב אֶל יֶ֣תֶר חֹֽתְנ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וְאָשׁ֨וּבָה֙ אֶל אַחַ֣י אֲשֶׁר בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶרְאֶ֖ה הַעוֹדָ֣ם חַיִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יִתְר֛וֹ לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses in Midian, Go, return to Egypt, for all the men seeking your life are dead.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.

modern.text: Now the LORD had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּמִדְיָ֔ן לֵ֖ךְ שֻׁ֣ב מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּי מֵ֨תוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ

verses.restored: Moses took his wife and sons, set them on the donkey, and returned to land of Egypt; and Moses took staff of the Divine in his hand.

familiar.text: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.

modern.text: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת אִשְׁתּ֣וֹ וְאֶת בָּנָ֗יו וַיַּרְכִּבֵם֙ עַֽל הַחֲמֹ֔ר וַיָּ֖שָׁב אַ֣רְצָה מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת מַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, When you go to return to Egypt, see all the wonders that I put in your hand, and do them before Pharaoh; but I will strengthen/harden his heart, and he will not send the people.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, When thou goest to return into Egypt, see that thou do all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.

modern.text: The LORD instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל מֹשֶׁה֒ בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִצְרַ֔יְמָה רְאֵ֗ה כָּל הַמֹּֽפְתִים֙ אֲשֶׁר שַׂ֣מְתִּי בְיָדֶ֔ךָ וַעֲשִׂיתָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַאֲנִי֙ אֲחַזֵּ֣ק אֶת לִבּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת הָעָֽם

verses.restored: You shall say to Pharaoh, Thus says YHWH: Israel is my son, my firstborn.

familiar.text: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn:

modern.text: Then tell Pharaoh that this is what the LORD says: ‘Israel is My firstborn son,

original.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֑ה כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּנִ֥י בְכֹרִ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: And I said to you, Send my son so he may serve/worship me; but you refused to send him. Look, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.

familiar.text: And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.

modern.text: and I told you to let My son go so that he may worship Me. But since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!’”

original.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יךָ שַׁלַּ֤ח אֶת בְּנִי֙ וְיַֽעַבְדֵ֔נִי וַתְּמָאֵ֖ן לְשַׁלְּח֑וֹ הִנֵּה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י הֹרֵ֔ג אֶת בִּנְךָ֖ בְּכֹרֶֽךָ

verses.restored: And it happened on the way, at the lodging place, that YHWH met him and sought to put him to death.

familiar.text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him.

modern.text: Now at a lodging place along the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֥י בַדֶּ֖רֶךְ בַּמָּל֑וֹן וַיִּפְגְּשֵׁ֣הוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ הֲמִיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Zipporah took a flint, cut the foreskin of her son, touched his feet, and said, Surely a bridegroom of bloods you are to me.

familiar.text: Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.

modern.text: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֨ח צִפֹּרָ֜ה צֹ֗ר וַתִּכְרֹת֙ אֶת עָרְלַ֣ת בְּנָ֔הּ וַתַּגַּ֖ע לְרַגְלָ֑יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֧י חֲתַן דָּמִ֛ים אַתָּ֖ה לִֽי

verses.restored: And he let him alone. Then she said, Bridegroom of bloods, because of circumcisions.

familiar.text: So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.

modern.text: So the LORD let him alone. (When she said, “bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.) The People Believe Moses and Aaron

translation_notes: Moses' speech objection is preserved without mocking disability; Divine response is presence with mouth and Aaron as support.
Hardening language begins here and requires careful tracking across Exodus; rendered strengthen/harden where Hebrew hazaq/kaved/qashah distinctions need later audit.
Israel firstborn language frames the confrontation with Pharaoh's firstborn policy from chapter 1.
Zipporah's circumcision episode is difficult and anciently obscure; preserve ambiguity and avoid overconfident interpretation.
safety_note: Exodus 4 contains dangerous and obscure death/circumcision material. Treat it as source-preserved, not as a ritual template. Do not use speech/disability material to shame Moses; the narrative provides Aaron as accommodation and partnership.
